page: The Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-800s-amd belongs to the Optimized Cloud Compute lineup and provides a memory-heavy configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. Compute resources are provided by dedicated AMD EPYC processors delivering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI cryptographic support, while AVX-512 and matrix extensions are absent. System memory is provisioned at 128 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio.

Storage is bundled directly with an 800 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, eliminating the latency of external network volumes for primary scratch and working datasets. Discrete GPU accelerators are not present. Performance metrics demonstrate competitive single-thread execution, where stress-ng single-core tests achieve top-decile placement. PassMark memory testing places in the upper quartile, supported by uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 135.4 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 68.38 GB/sec. Overall multi-core throughput, Geekbench metrics, and Redis benchmarks yielding 31.17 million SET operations per second reflect steady median-tier execution consistent with its 2.0 GHz base clock.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance provides high memory density coupled with high-speed local NVMe storage within a standard compute footprint. The omission of GPU hardware and advanced vector instruction sets makes it unsuitable for complex model training and dense matrix operations. However, the high RAM-to-CPU ratio makes it resource-efficient for environments where working datasets exceed typical general-purpose memory limits. Recommended workloads include transactional database hosting, distributed caching clusters such as Redis, large-scale ETL processing, search index nodes, and memory-intensive enterprise web services.
description: The Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-800s-amd is an x86_64 cloud server from the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.0 GHz. Built with a memory-dense footprint, it provisions 128 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, alongside a bundled 800 GB local NVMe solid-state drive and zero GPUs. Benchmark measurements reflect strong memory subsystem performance, supported by top-tier single-core stress-ng throughput and robust text generation rates in small language models, while multi-core processing and Redis operations remain firmly in the mid-tier category. The balance of high memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage delivers solid resource density without the premium overhead of specialized accelerator hardware. This profile is engineered for memory-heavy enterprise software, including relational databases, in-memory caches, data analytics pipelines, and memory-constrained web serving tasks.
